o: The moth's wings are patterned in shades of brown and gray.
The moth was observed feeding exclusively between 9 p.m. and 4 a.m.
The moth is roughly the same size as other moths in its genus.
The moth was first identified in a tropical rainforest.
PART_A.e: "Nocturnal" means active at night. Only the feeding-time observation (9 p.m.–4 a.m.) directly supports that claim; wing color, size, and habitat don't address activity timing.

PART_A.q: A city council debated a proposal to convert a downtown parking lot into a public park. Supporters cited increased foot traffic for nearby businesses; opponents worried about the loss of parking revenue. The council ultimately voted 5-2 to approve the conversion, with both dissenting members citing the parking concern. Based on the text, which statement is most strongly supported?
o: The council was unanimous in supporting the park.
Concerns about parking revenue were not persuasive enough to block the proposal.
The park was rejected due to insufficient support.
PART_A.e: A 5-2 vote in favor, with the dissent specifically about parking, shows the parking concern existed but didn't sway the majority — supporting that it "was not persuasive enough to block" approval.

PART_A.q: The town's old textile mill closed in 1987, and for decades the building sat vacant. ______, a local developer purchased the property last year and began converting it into artist studios. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
PART_A.e: The mill sat vacant for decades, but then something changed (a developer purchased it) — that shift in direction calls for a contrast word: "However."

PART_A.q:
A student is writing a report about coral bleaching and has taken the following notes:
• Coral bleaching occurs when corals expel the algae living in their tissues.
• The algae provide corals with food through photosynthesis and give them their color.
• Bleaching is often triggered by a rise in ocean temperature of just 1-2°C.
• Bleached coral is not dead but is more vulnerable to disease and starvation.
The student wants to explain why a small temperature change has such a large effect on coral. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Coral bleaching happens when corals expel algae, which changes the coral's color from bright to white.
Because corals depend on algae for food and color, a rise of just 1-2°C is enough to trigger the expulsion of that algae, leaving the coral vulnerable.
Bleached coral can still survive, though it becomes more likely to develop disease or starve.
Ocean temperatures have been rising steadily over the past several decades due to climate change.
PART_A.e: Only this choice connects the small temperature trigger (1-2°C) to WHY it matters — because the coral depends on the expelled algae for food and color — directly answering "why a small change has a large effect."

PART_A.q:
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

The committee reviewed three proposals; ______ was approved without revision.
PART_A.e: With three items, "none of them" is correct; "neither" only applies to exactly two options.

PART_A.q:
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

Each of the interns, having completed the mandatory training modules, ______ eligible to apply for a full-time position.
PART_A.e: "Each" is singular and is the subject (the phrase "of the interns" is a modifier), so the verb must agree with "each": "is."

PART_A.q: Despite the coach's ______ approach, the team's performance improved steadily throughout the season. Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?
PART_A.e: Steady improvement over a season fits a careful, detail-oriented ("meticulous") coaching approach; the other options suggest inconsistency or disengagement, which wouldn't produce steady gains.

PART_A.q: A nutritionist argues that a particular diet improves sleep quality. Which piece of evidence would most weaken this claim?
o: Participants on the diet reported feeling more energetic during the day.
A control group not on the diet showed the same improvement in sleep quality.
The diet was followed for eight consecutive weeks.
Participants kept a daily food journal during the study.
PART_A.e: If a control group NOT on the diet improved just as much, that suggests the diet itself isn't what caused the improvement — directly undermining the claim.

PART_A.q: The novel received mixed reviews upon its initial release, with several critics dismissing its nonlinear structure as confusing. ______, it has since been reevaluated as a landmark of experimental fiction. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
PART_A.e: Mixed/negative reception followed by later praise is a contrast, so "Nevertheless" fits; "Consequently" would wrongly imply the reevaluation was a result of the criticism.

PART_A.q: A historian's essay opens by describing a widely believed myth about a historical event, then spends the remaining paragraphs presenting archival evidence that contradicts the myth. What is the primary purpose of the opening paragraph?
o: To establish the essay's overall argument as fact
To provide a claim the essay will go on to challenge
To summarize the historian's own research methods
To introduce an unrelated topic for contrast
PART_A.e: An opening that states a common belief, followed by evidence against it, functions as a claim being set up for the essay to refute — not as an established fact or a methods summary.

PART_A.q:
A student has gathered the following notes about two renewable energy sources:
• Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity and have no moving parts.
• Wind turbines have moving parts that require regular maintenance.
• Solar panels produce no electricity at night.
• Wind turbines can generate power at any hour, as long as wind speeds are sufficient.
The student wants to compare a key trade-off between the two technologies. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Solar panels are simpler, with no moving parts, but produce no power at night, whereas wind turbines can generate electricity at any hour but need more maintenance.
Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity, while wind turbines rely on wind speed.
Both solar panels and wind turbines are considered renewable energy sources.
Wind turbines have moving parts, which solar panels do not have.
PART_A.e: Only this choice states an actual trade-off (simplicity/no night power vs. maintenance/anytime power) — synthesizing two notes on each side rather than just restating isolated facts.

PART_A.q:
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

The museum's newest exhibit features artifacts from ancient Egypt, Greece, and Rome______ each displayed in its own gallery.
PART_A.e: "With each displayed in its own gallery" is a modifying phrase describing how the artifacts are shown — it should be set off with a comma, not a semicolon (which requires an independent clause).

PART_B1.q:
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

The data, collected over a period of five years, ______ a clear downward trend in the river's water level.
PART_B1.e: "Data" is the (plural) subject; "collected over a period of five years" is a modifying phrase, not the subject. The verb should agree with the plural "data": "show."

PART_B1.q: The negotiations, once ______, resumed only after both sides agreed to bring in a neutral mediator. Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?
PART_B1.e: Needing a mediator to resume implies the talks had stopped — "stalled" fits; the other options don't imply a breakdown requiring intervention.

PART_B1.q: The city's new bike-share program placed 200 bicycles at 40 stations across downtown. Within the first month, ridership exceeded projections by 60%, prompting officials to plan an expansion to residential neighborhoods. Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
o: A bike-share program in one city failed to meet expectations.
A city's bike-share program saw stronger-than-expected use and is being expanded.
Bike-share programs are more popular in downtown areas than in residential ones.
The city plans to remove its bike-share stations.
PART_B1.e: The text reports higher-than-projected ridership and a planned expansion — success and growth, not failure or removal.

PART_B1.q: A company's internal memo states that the marketing budget for next quarter will be "consistent with this quarter's spending, adjusted for the launch of two new product lines." Based on the memo, which is the most reasonable inference?
o: The marketing budget will decrease significantly next quarter.
The marketing budget next quarter will likely be higher than this quarter's.
The company is discontinuing its current product lines.
The marketing budget will remain exactly the same next quarter.
PART_B1.e: "Consistent... adjusted for the launch of two new product lines" implies additional spending to support the new launches — most reasonably meaning the budget will rise, not stay flat or fall.

PART_B1.q: The bridge was originally designed to carry only pedestrian traffic. ______, as the surrounding neighborhood grew, city planners reinforced it to accommodate light vehicles. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
PART_B1.e: The bridge's original limited purpose changed due to later reinforcement — a shift best signaled by the contrast word "However."

PART_B1.q:
A student has gathered the following notes about two note-taking methods:
• The Cornell method divides a page into sections for notes, cues, and a summary.
• Studies show the Cornell method improves recall when students review the summary section weekly.
• Mind mapping uses branching diagrams to visually connect related ideas.
• Mind mapping is often preferred for brainstorming and seeing relationships between topics.
The student wants to recommend Cornell note-taking specifically for exam review. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Mind mapping uses branching diagrams to connect ideas visually.
The Cornell method's built-in summary section, when reviewed weekly, has been shown to improve recall — making it well suited for exam review.
Both note-taking methods can be useful depending on the student's preference.
Mind mapping is generally preferred for brainstorming sessions.
PART_B1.e: Only this choice connects a specific feature (the summary section) to a proven benefit (improved recall) that directly supports recommending it FOR EXAM REVIEW — the student's stated goal.

PART_B1.q:
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

The report outlined three main findings______ rising costs, declining enrollment, and outdated facilities.
PART_B1.e: A colon correctly introduces a list that elaborates on "three main findings." A semicolon requires an independent clause on both sides, which this isn't.

PART_B1.q:
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

Neither the manager nor the employees ______ aware of the policy change until it was announced.
PART_B1.e: With "neither...nor," the verb agrees with the noun closer to it — "employees" (plural) — so "were" is correct.

PART_B1.q: The senator's speech was carefully ______, avoiding any direct commitment while still appearing responsive to constituents' concerns. Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?
PART_B1.e: Avoiding direct commitment while appearing responsive describes deliberately vague language — "evasive" fits precisely; the other options all suggest directness or spontaneity, the opposite.

PART_B1.q: An article begins by describing a common misconception about a species of spider, then explains the biological reality, and closes by noting why the misconception persists in popular culture. What is the function of the article's final paragraph?
o: To restate the misconception as true
To explain the origin or persistence of a belief the article has just corrected
To introduce a new, unrelated misconception
To question the biological evidence presented earlier
PART_B1.e: A closing paragraph explaining why a just-corrected misconception persists is explaining the belief's origin/persistence — not restating it as true or undermining the article's own evidence.

PART_B1.q: A city planner claims that adding a bike lane on Main Street reduced car traffic congestion. Which finding would most directly support this claim?
o: Average commute times on Main Street decreased by 15% after the bike lane was added.
The bike lane cost $200,000 to install.
Main Street is two miles long.
Local businesses reported mixed opinions about the bike lane.
PART_B1.e: A direct decrease in commute times after installation is the most direct evidence that congestion actually decreased; cost, length, and business opinions don't measure congestion.

PART_B1.q: Early drafts of the policy included a provision for extended review periods. ______, the final version removed this provision to speed up implementation. Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
PART_B1.e: "Ultimately" signals the final outcome after the earlier drafts — a fitting transition to describe what the final version did, in contrast to the early drafts.

PART_B1.q:
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

The committee's recommendation—though controversial among some board members—______ ultimately adopted without further amendment.
PART_B1.e: The subject is "recommendation" (singular); the dashes set off a parenthetical ("though controversial among some board members") that doesn't change subject-verb agreement. "Was" is correct.
